description: Tier 2 adversarial routing suite — semantic prompts that deliberately avoid the skill's obvious trigger keywords, to measure whether routing works on meaning rather than vocabulary. Consumed by scripts/eval-routing.py (stdlib) alongside tier2-routing-evals.json; schema-compatible with the node runner.

suites.description: Paraphrased, keyword-poor prompts: the correct skill must still win, and near-neighbour skills must not be falsely activated

scenarios.input: We acquired a competitor and now need to bring two separate codebases and two git histories into one repository
A third of our CI runs fail on tests that pass locally, and the failing test moves around run to run
Finance says our cloud bill tripled this quarter; find which workload is responsible and how we cap it
Production is down and customers are seeing errors; we need to find the root cause fast and coordinate the fix
Every week the main table gets bigger and our queries get slower and slower
Two teammates keep editing the same lines and we lose work at every merge
A user asked us to erase everything we hold about them and we need a defensible, auditable process
Clients want to fetch exactly the fields they need instead of huge fixed REST responses; move us over gradually
We have hundreds of thousands of lines nobody is sure are still used; find what we can safely remove
A large enterprise customer demands proof of our security controls before they will sign
Someone dropped a production table by accident; get the data back with as little loss as possible
I need a second pair of eyes that only reads code and never edits it, to approve a risky refactor before merge
Rename an endpoint path and update every caller across all our services without breaking deploys
Before we build anything, we need to know whether this market is worth entering and who the real competitors are
